steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).

To make the pie: Whisk sugar, flour, and salt together in a mixing bowl. Add sour cream, egg, and vanilla; beat with an electric mixer until combined. Stir in sliced peaches. Pour mixture into pie crust.

Bake in the preheated oven for 12 minutes. Reduce the oven temperature to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) and continue baking until the filling is set, about 30 minutes. Remove from the oven; increase the oven temperature to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
To make the topping: Whisk flour, sugar, and cinnamon together in a small bowl. Mix in butter with a fork until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Sprinkle crumb topping evenly over pie.
Return the pie to the oven and bake until topping is golden, about 10 minutes. Let pie cool slightly before slicing, about 15 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Old-Fashioned Peach Cream Pie
raw_recipe.description: Have a hankering for an old-fashioned peach cream pie? This recipe pairs fresh peaches with a tangy vanilla custard under a decadent cinnamon crumble.
raw_recipe.name: Old-Fashioned Peach Cream Pie

review.reviewBody: This is a very tasty recipe. I thought the topping was just a little too sweet, so next time I may cut back a little on the sugar. Also, I used a deeper pie plate so I will increase the amount of filling, including adding more peaches. It does puff up during baking, then settles back in. I did sprinkle some cinnamon on the peach filling before baking also. This is even better when cooled in the refrigerator. Thanks for a great recipe. I will definately make it again in the summer with some fresh peaches! FOOTNOTE: My father-in-law thought this was one of the best peach pies he's ever had!

I doubled the recipe to make two pies and baked both at the same time. I followed the directions step-by-step, but I was a little short on sour cream, so I probably only put about a cup-and-a-half of sour cream in them. I also used about 12 fresh peaches (6 peaches per pie). While baking the first 42 mins., I covered the edges of the pie crust. I followed Trinity's Mom's suggestion and added some oats to the topping. The pies were out of the oven for 15-20 mins. while I prepared the topping and upped the temp. to 400 degrees again, and when I put them back in the oven I uncovered the edges for the last 10 mins., then turned the oven off and let them sit in the oven for another 10 mins. They were perfect; not runny at all. I cooled them for about 40 mins. and then covered them and put them in the fridge to chill, and they were delicious!! Thanks for a great recipe!!

Pie turned out great and not too sweet - I cut back on the sugar in the custard by 1/4 cup. Other modifications: I split the sugar for the crumble with brown sugar and white sugar, added 2 Tbsp oats. To the pie I added more sliced peaches (as much as it could hold), and added 1/2 Tsp. more vanilla. I used a store bought crust and pre baked it for 8 minutes - I think this prevented the bottom of the crust from being too soggy. Would definitely make again and perfect for tea time during the summer!

This is a great pie. One problem I had it with the topping. There seemed to be too much butter in it. When mixed it wanted to clump into one big ball, when cooked it took about 40 minutes to get to a point where I could take it out of the oven. It never completely browned, or maybe it did but the cinnamon disguised it. Anyway, the top was swimming in butter. One other thing, I had to add more peaches to the peach mixture. After it was in the pie shell I noticed that there was a lot of places where there were no peaches. Fortunately I had thawed out an extra bag and probably added an additional cup. You can follow this recipe and add any extra peaches while it is in the pie shell. This is a great pie but next time I will start off with 1/8 cup of butter. I will certainly make it again.

I had some frozen, fresh peaches & wanted to make a Peach Cream pie like my Mom used to make. I don't have her recipe, but this was close. I made several changes, since I usually don't have everything on hand. I substituted Coconut sugar for regular sugar, so it was a little browner than usual. I also only used 1/3 cup coconut sugar in the pie & plain greek yogurt instead of sour cream. I also used a graham cracker crust I had on hand. I added some oats to the topping. It was very good warm.

This was yum! I did change a couple of things - I did a mix of apple and peach (what I had on hand) and I increased the fruit content to a little over double the recipe to make sure the crust was filled and also that it had enough fruit compared to cream. I also used plain Greek yogurt in place of the sour cream as I had some that needed using. I loved this pie - it was the perfect mix of sweet fruit pie with a little twang to stop it being too sweet. I will make again I am sure.

Delicious! I doubled the recipe and used peaches with blueberries in one and peaches with raspberries in the other. I used regular pie pans (not deep dish) and 6 fresh peaches. I ended up leaving them in the oven much longer than the 30 min suggested (I think 45 in total) and the custard never fully set. It was definitely better after a chill in the refrigerator (too runny when warm). I also listened to others and cut the sugar amount in the topping. I think next time, less butter would be better too. I like a more crumbly top. all in all - I give it a 4.5 stars.
I did substitute plain greek yogurt for sour cream and added extra peaches and some oats to the topping. It was delicious and smelled awesome!

Wonderful recipe! The only addition was fresh ground nutmeg as I like the nutmeg peach combination. I put the crumb topping on the pie right away and left the oven at 400 for 40 minutes. Beautiful pie.

I'd never heard of a peach cream pie before and with it being late summer peach season, this recipe sounded delicious. It was very easy to make and it didn't disappoint. The sour cream added a tangy dimension to what can sometimes be a one note fruit pie. I followed the directions to the T with one small exception--I added a couple dashes of nutmeg & clove to the topping. My only issue was it required an extra 15 minutes of baking to set. Even then, while it was not runny, it would have been better if it were a bit more firm. Next time I would use only 3/4 sour cream. It was also a little too sweet for me. I would recommend cutting the sugar by 1/4 cup. That would make this pie perfect!

first it is a wonderful recipe, but like all the wonderful chefs that comment and adjust the fantastic recipe first I thought it was to peachy.. so I removed the peaches and add potatoes. Then I removed the sugar because it did not make sense to add that to my potatoes so I added mayonnaise. Then instead of flour, I added some onions. But first I cubed and cooked both the onions and potatoes in some butter. Then once cooked I mixed with the mayo, added some salt and pepper and put in the fridge. I would do this again, and picking potatoes fresh off the tree is the best!

This is the same as an apple version I just made, except no sugar is added to sour cream, egg and flour filling. Cannot imagine why so much extra sugar is needed in filling, unless using something like rhubarb. Checked other sour cream pies on this site, all seem to add a cup or more sugar to filling. Glad I did not, sweet topping sufficient.
It took alittle longer in the oven, but turned out great! Will make it again!!
This is one of my families favorites. They always ask for me to make it!
I used 8oz cream cheese instead of the sour cream. It was delicious.
